Dark theme visibility fixes across checkboxes, toggles and progress bars, the Event Scripter script editor working again under the Dark theme, and a fix for the crash loop some setups hit after updating. Just **force update**; your `/config` is untouched.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Event Scripter script editor now opens on the Dark theme.** The Event Scripter extension's script editor (edit and Add script) did nothing while the Dark theme was active: the editor window never opened, so scripts could not be edited or added. Two latent NullPointerExceptions in JDownloader/AppWork code surface only under the FlatLaf dark look-and-feel and were swallowed silently, aborting the editor dialog before it could show: AppWork's `CircledProgressBar` UI dereferenced a null back-reference during layout when FlatLaf re-created the transient progress widget, and jsyntaxpane's `ScriptAction` dereferenced a null `javax.script` engine (the current Java runtime ships no built-in JavaScript engine) while installing the code-editor kit. The container's in-process agent now guards both at the root with a load-time bytecode transform, so the editor opens without changing the Carbon `#161616` dark theme in any way. The guard is fail-safe: if the guarded code ever changes upstream, the original behaviour is used unchanged. (Reported on the Unraid forum, thanks kayn.)
- **Unchecked checkboxes were nearly invisible.** On the dark `#161616` theme an unchecked checkbox (and radio button) had almost no visible outline. The border is now a clear light grey, so an empty box reads just as well as a ticked one.
- **The package expand/collapse toggle (`[+]` / `[-]`) rendered black.** After a JDownloader self-update the little toggle next to a package could turn black and vanish on the dark background. It is now always drawn in light grey.
- **Download progress bars flashed grey while scrolling.** Scrolling a package's file list briefly greyed out some progress bars. The bar fill is now unified, so scrolling no longer causes a grey flash.
- **Black screen / crash loop after updating (`UnsupportedClassVersionError`).** A dependency bump compiled the container's dialog-agent (`jd-dialog-agent.jar`) with Java 25, but JDownloader itself runs on the Java 21 runtime. The Java 21 JVM refused to load the newer agent class (`class file version 69.0`, this runtime only reads up to `65.0`), aborted the `-javaagent` at startup, and the autostart kept relaunching JDownloader into a black screen. The agent is now compiled with `javac --release 21`, so it always targets the runtime's Java version regardless of which JDK builds the image.

## ⚡ Improved

- **CI can no longer let a broken agent through.** The image's smoke test used to pass the moment JDownloader's JVM started, but that log line prints just before a bad `-javaagent` would abort it, so a broken build could go green. The gate now fails on JVM/agent crash signatures and on a relaunch loop, and requires the JVM to stay up before publishing, so a dialog-agent that can't load the runtime can never reach the published image again.
